name: cloud-ide
description: Cloud-IDE — constellation of three minimally-forked upstream developer apps (Acode code editor / Amaze File Manager / Amaze File Utilities) plus a thin original hub APK. The hub switches between the forks and brokers their data (workspaces, recent files, git status, storage analysis, transfers) to Cloud-SuperApp over signature-gated AIDL + ContentProvider IPC. The shared resource is a hub-owned on-device workspace tree (not a server). Forks are declarative: pinned upstream tag + committed patch series, materialized into gitignored tracker clones at build time. Built via Nix devShell (gradle + AGP + Android SDK + node/cordova for the Acode fork).

android._doc: Hub-only application coordinates. The forks carry their OWN applicationId / version (declared per fork in build.json::forks) — they are separate APKs.
android._doc_abi_filters: Hub is pure-JVM (no native libs) so ABI filtering is irrelevant to it; kept for schema parity with ea_cloud-superapp / ea_cloud-comms. The forks declare their own abi_filters.

signing._doc: Stable SHARED Cloud-constellation signing key — the same key signs SuperApp / Cloud-Nav / Cloud-Comms / Cloud-IDE so cross-app installs + the in-app updater never hit a signature mismatch. The keystore (raw credential) + passwords live ONLY in vault; only these non-secret path refs are here. build.sh::_resolve_signing resolves $VAULT_DIR (default ~/git/vault) + sops-decrypts vault_secrets, exporting ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE / ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD / ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS / ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD which the gradle signingConfig reads. CI does the same via a vault checkout + the SOPS_AGE_KEY secret. Without the vault key (pure-local dev) gradle falls back to the legacy debug keystore. Paths relative to the vault repo root.
signing._disabled_2026_06_24: vault/shared-key signing DISABLED — it signed OU=Cloud Constellation (wrong key c0f94b17), poisoned GHCR and broke installs on every device. Empty vault_keystore => _resolve_signing returns early => legacy per-app keystore (the canonical published key). Do NOT restore without a deliberate full re-key + one-time reinstall on every device.

toolchain._doc: Pinned for reproducibility — all derived in flake.nix. Mirrors ea_cloud-superapp / ea_cloud-comms pins so all the Android projects share one toolchain story. Node is added for the Acode (Cordova) fork's JS/plugin build.

ipc._doc: Single source of truth for the on-device IPC surface. Kotlin constants in hub + SuperApp + every fork exporter MUST mirror this; contract/ide-ipc-v1.json carries the full table/aidl shapes and is validated by `./build.sh verify-contract`. Bumping `version` is a breaking change — add an ide-ipc-v2.json, never edit v1 in place. The permission/authority share the com.diegonmarcos.ide namespace; the signature on this permission is the SAME constellation key as cloud-comms + ea_cloud-superapp.

ui._doc: Hub UI defaults baked into BuildConfig. overlay_nav_bar_default: the floating cross-app wrapper bar (NavOverlayService) is DISABLED by default — Cloud-SuperApp now owns the system-wide bar. The code stays; Configs has a toggle (persisted in prefs) for users who run Cloud-IDE standalone.

modules._doc: Gradle module graph — settings.gradle iterates this (FIRE rule 6: never hardcode the list). Only the hub is an in-tree gradle module; the three forks are SEPARATE gradle/cordova projects living in their materialized tracker clones, built via `./build.sh build-fork <name>`, never included here.

hub.comment: Thin switcher + IPC broker. Original code (no upstream). Declares the signature permission, the unified IdeProvider (reads), the IIdeService AIDL (actions + push callbacks), the launcher switcher UI, and owns the shared workspace root (data/ide-endpoints.json::workspace.root_path). HUB-SHARING: the broker + updater are structurally identical to cloud-comms-hub — once both exist, extract them into a shared gradle module (see forks/../README) rather than maintaining two copies. cloud-comms scaffolded first, so Cloud-IDE consumes the extracted core; until that extraction lands, this hub mirrors the comms hub deliberately.

forks._doc: Declarative fork registry — THE source of truth. OWNER DECISION (2026-06-11): Cloud-IDE is a WRAPPER — exactly TWO apps, Acode + Amaze File Manager, ride SELF-CONTAINED inside the hub APK (forks with an `embedded` block; seeded by `build.sh bundle-forks` from the pinned upstream release URL + sha256). The HOME shows ONLY embedded forks (two tiles, display_name) — `utils` has no embedded block and is NOT on the home (kept for the future patched-fork phase). Each fork = pinned tag + patch series for the LATER owned-fork phase (materialize-fork/build-fork unchanged). `embedded.package` = the id the bundled APK installs as; launching + <queries> use it. Tags + sha256 verified live 2026-06-11.

embedded._doc: SELF-CONTAINED bundle. source=build → bundle-forks builds OUR patched fork (build-fork files → dist/cloud-ide-files.apk, package com.diegonmarcos.ide.files, our top nav bar baked in) and embeds it at assets/forks/files.apk. `url`+`sha256` remain as the upstream fallback when the build toolchain is absent (e.g. CI without rust/ndk — until fork-ship-to-GHCR). `package` is the install id used by launch + <queries>.

build._doc: build-fork settings for OUR patched APK (pin + patch series → com.diegonmarcos.ide.files with the baked-in top nav bar). fdroid flavor; release signed by the cloudide config (patch 0001). `keystore` is generated by build-fork before gradle (keytool, debug-default password 'android') if absent — relative to the tracker root.

files.comment: Amaze File Manager. Build this fork FIRST: native Kotlin/Java, core of the file domain. PAIRING: FM hardcodes the Utilities package in AboutActivity.PACKAGE_AMAZE_UTILS = 'com.amaze.fileutilities' (launch constant) and reads its intent extra 'com.amaze.fileutilities.AFM_LOCATE_FILE_NAME' in MainActivity — both must be renamed symmetrically with the utils fork. Exporter FilesExportProvider owns recent_files + transfers. Uses MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (self-distributed, no Play policy).

utils.comment: Amaze File Utilities. Build SECOND (smallest diff, but must follow files for the symmetric pairing rename). Upstream is near-dormant (v1.94, 2024-07) — lowest drift cost, effectively owned. Already ships AIDL. Exporter UtilsExportProvider owns storage_summary. Re-namespace its FM-targeted intent key AFM_LOCATE_FILE_NAME to match the files fork's MainActivity reader.

embedded._doc: SELF-CONTAINED bundle: the REAL upstream Acode FOSS release APK rides inside the hub (assets/forks/editor.apk). Package id confirmed from upstream config.xml widget id. Same mechanism as files.embedded.

editor.comment: Acode code editor (Cordova hybrid, MIT). Build LAST: fastest-moving upstream (~weekly; v1.12.4 was latest at scaffold). Keep the NATIVE patch diff minimal — applicationId/branding + ONE Cordova plugin (Java) declaring the EditorExportProvider + IIdeService stub via <config-file target=AndroidManifest.xml> in plugin.xml. ALL behavior (recent-file reporting, workspace registration, hub switcher entry, gitea/SFTP presets) lives in forks/editor/acode-plugin/ as a normal Acode JS plugin so it rides upstream updates for free. Built-in SFTP gets presets from data/ide-endpoints.json. Exporter owns workspaces + recent_files + git_repos.

release._doc: Per-APK distribution for the HUB — SAME data-driven pattern as ea_cloud-superapp / ea_cloud-comms build.json::release. build.sh oras-push + gh-release read this block; the GHA workflow (1_workflows/src/cicd/ship-cloud-ide.yml) only invokes those engine commands, no hardcoded registry/tag strings. The three forks publish their own OCI artifacts under their own build systems. {sha} → git short sha, {version_name} → android.version_name.

abis._doc: ABI build axis. The hub is pure-JVM (ABI-agnostic); the ONLY native-bearing bundled app is the patched Amaze fork (Rust :file_operations). `build.sh build [abi]` / `build-fork <k> [abi]` / `bundle-forks [abi]` select one. `default:true` is what bare `build` / the CI artifact use; non-default abis get a -<abi> artifact suffix. rust_target = the rust-android-gradle cargo target key (passed as -PcloudIdeRustTargets).

artifact._doc: Path under dist/ to publish. `debug` is the daily-driver build (no ProGuard, real stacktraces, debug keystore) — THE hub app, not a side-by-side variant. asset_name matches `debug` so the engine skips a redundant copy.

ghcr._doc: ORAS push as an OCI artifact (APK is a blob, not a container). One :latest tag plus per-commit sha + per-version tags.

gh_release._doc: GitHub Release attachment. rolling_tag is canonical: one release (default `latest`) the ship workflow overwrites on every main push, so /releases/latest/download/Cloud-IDE-Hub.apk is a stable URL. tag_pattern stays for immutable per-tag releases under a tag push (rolling release publishes alongside).

phone_install._doc: Targets for build.sh phone-install — pulls the hub APK from GHCR via curl+OCI HTTP API (no oras dep; works on aarch64 Termux without a Nix shell) and copies it where an Android file manager can see it. Override per-env via PHONE_TARGET.

auto_update._doc: In-app updater config — read at gradle eval time into BuildConfig, then used by the hub's com.diegonmarcos.ide.update package at runtime (same OCI HTTP flow as build.sh oras-pull). Same registry/namespace/image as release.ghcr. The hub self-updates from cloud-ide-hub:<tag>; the forks update via the same mechanism once they publish their own images. Mirrors ea_cloud-superapp/build.json::release.auto_update.
auto_update._doc_interval: WorkManager periodic minimum is 15 min. 6h matches typical update cadence + spares battery / data.
auto_update._doc_install: 'prompt' uses PackageInstaller with a user confirmation per Android's security model. 'silent' would need the system updater privilege (F-Droid Privileged Extension territory).
